generatedProse.concept-context: The three parts of this course are one practice, not three separate tricks. A structure gives reflection its stages; critical reflection does the real work inside the reflect stage by asking why; and a concrete action closes the cycle so it changes what you do. In any subject, skilled reflective practice is simply these three working together: a shape to follow, a why to dig into, and a definite next step to carry forward.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Consider two students reflecting on the same placement day, which went poorly.

Student A uses a structure and describes each stage neatly, but the reflect stage only restates what happened, and the action, to be more confident, is a wish. The shape is there without the substance; the cycle turns but changes nothing.

Student B follows the same structure, then reflects with an edge: the day went poorly because they had not read the brief and so kept deferring to others. From that why comes a concrete action, to read the next brief the evening before and arrive with two questions ready. Structure, critical reflection and a usable action, all three, working as one. That is reflective practice rather than a reflective form filled in.

Both used a cycle. Only Student B made it a practice.
generatedProse.summary: Reflective practice is a structure, critical reflection and a concrete action working as one: a shape to follow, a why to dig into, and a definite next step. You can now recognise skilled reflective practice when you see it, analyse how its parts support each other, and bring all three to bear on your own work. That is a habit worth keeping well beyond this course.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Student B's work reflective practice rather than a reflective form filled in?

items.text: Student B combined the structure with a real why and a concrete action.
Student B followed the structure more neatly than Student A.
Student B described each stage in more detail.
Student B felt more confident about the placement.

feedback.correct: Yes. Practice is the three parts working together: structure, a real why, and a usable action.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Both used the structure; look for where Student B adds a real why and a concrete action.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Student B made it a practice by joining the structure to a genuine why and a usable action. A neater form, more detail or more confidence are not the same.

The merge renders it as a block quote, so write it as continuous prose, not as a quoted comment plus commentary.
